sentences.en: This is a moment to seize.
sentences.zh: 这是一个需要把握的时刻。

sentences.en: The kaleidoscope has been shaken.
sentences.zh: 万花筒已被摇动。

sentences.en: The pieces are in flux.
sentences.zh: 碎片正在流转。

sentences.en: Soon they will settle again.
sentences.zh: 很快它们将再度安定下来。

sentences.en: Before they do, let us reorder this world around us.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，让我们重新整理身边的这个世界。

sentences.en: That was Tony Blair on the 2nd of October 2001, five days before the American and British invasion of Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 那是托尼·布莱尔在2001年10月2日的发言，也就是美英入侵阿富汗的前五天。

sentences.en: And now we all know how that story ended up.
sentences.zh: 现在我们都知道那个故事是以什么结局收场了。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we thought we would devote this week's podcast to a survey of Afghan history, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我们觉得本周的播客可以用来纵览一下阿富汗的历史，对吧？

sentences.en: Explain some of the background to the events that we've been seeing in the last few days and to ask some of these sort of big questions about can empires ever intervene in Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 解释一下我们这几天所见事件的一些背景，并探讨一些宏观问题，比如帝国是否真的能干预阿富汗？

sentences.en: Is it an inherently lawless and violent place or is that just a series of kind of cliches?
sentences.zh: 这里是一个生来就无法无天、充满暴力的地方，还是说那只是一系列陈词滥调？

sentences.en: And also, this episode will serve as an introduction to a much more focused episode,
sentences.zh: 而且，本期节目也将作为下一期更聚焦内容的铺垫，

sentences.en: which will follow tomorrow with Willie Dalrymple looking specifically at the episode that people often kind of compare to what's going on today, which is the first Afghan war,
sentences.zh: 明天威利·达尔林普尔将带来后续节目，专门探讨人们经常拿来与今天的情况作类比的那段历史，也就是第一次阿富汗战争，

sentences.en: absolutely calamitous disaster in the history of British imperialism.
sentences.zh: 英国帝国主义历史上绝对惨绝人寰的灾难。

sentences.en: But yes, but I do think that the talk of Afghanistan as a graveyard of empires, of which obviously, for obvious reasons, there's a great deal at the moment,
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，我认为把阿富汗称为“帝国的坟墓”这种说法——眼下由于显而易见的原因，这种言论到处都是——

sentences.en: occludes the way in which Afghanistan has also been a great womb of empires.
sentences.zh: 它掩盖了阿富汗同时也是“帝国温床”的这一事实。

sentences.en: If you pull the camera back, this way in which imperial powers kind of gestate within Afghanistan, and then they kind of come out down the Khyber Pass, invade northern India,
sentences.zh: 如果你把镜头拉远，就会发现帝国势力正是在阿富汗境内孕育，然后通过开伯尔山口涌出，入侵印度北部，

sentences.en: settle there, become kind of innovated and soft, and then the cycle repeats.
sentences.zh: 在那里定居，变得因革新而腐化软弱，接着周而复始。

sentences.en: I mean, that's an equally kind of resonant pattern that you can trace through history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这也是一种同样具有深远意义、贯穿历史的模式。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此，不是吗？

sentences.en: And also, when people say, oh, they talk about the sort of medieval barbarism of the Taliban and so on.
sentences.zh: 还有，当人们说，哦，他们谈论塔利班的某种中世纪野蛮行径等等。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, the irony is that in medieval period, Afghanistan was actually a very sophisticated and civilized place.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其实讽刺的是，在中世纪时期，阿富汗实际上是一个非常成熟和文明的地方。

sentences.en: And indeed, an ancient history as well.
sentences.zh: 而且在古代历史上也是如此。

sentences.en: So let's put it into a bit of context.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们把它放回具体的语境中来看。

sentences.en: And actually, I know we both agree about this, that the single most important thing is to get a sense of geography, because geography comes before history, famously.
sentences.zh: 其实，我知道我们俩都同意这一点，那就是最重要的事情是建立对地理的感知，因为众所周知，地理决定历史。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so actually, as we're sitting here, I've got a map right in front of me.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们坐在这里时，我的面前就放着一张地图。

sentences.en: And crucially, it doesn't just show the cities, it shows the mountains.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，它不仅显示了城市，还显示了山脉。

sentences.en: Because Afghanistan is quite a kind of odd country.
sentences.zh: 因为阿富汗是一个相当奇特的国家。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not, I think, a kind of natural nation state in the way, say, that England might be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为它并不是一个像英格兰那样自然的民族国家。

sentences.en: Denmark.
sentences.zh: 丹麦。

sentences.en: Denmark.
sentences.zh: 丹麦。

sentences.en: You can trace the contour.
sentences.zh: 你能勾勒出它的轮廓。

sentences.en: So Afghanistan has a massive range of mountains running right the way through the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 所以阿富汗境内有一条巨大的山脉直接贯穿中部。

sentences.en: And the key cities kind of basically exist in relationship to that.
sentences.zh: 而主要的城市基本上都围绕着这些山脉分布。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the northern kind of flatlands, the north of these mountain range, in very ancient times, was known as Bactria.
sentences.zh: 所以北部的平原，也就是山脉以北地区，在远古时期被称为巴克特里亚。

sentences.en: And the southern range, the kind of deserts that you have there, were known as Arakozia.
sentences.zh: 而南部的山脉和那里的沙漠，则被称为阿拉霍西亚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you've got Herat in the far weSt.
sentences.zh: 所以极西边有赫拉特。

sentences.en: You've got Kandahar in the far south.
sentences.zh: 极南边有坎大哈。

sentences.en: And you've got Kabul in a kind of a valley, which it links to what is now Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 而喀布尔则位于一个山谷中，它连接着现在的巴基斯坦。

sentences.en: But you have these massive mountains in the middle.
sentences.zh: 但中间有这些巨大的山脉。

sentences.en: And that is really the kind of the key factor, I think, that you have to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是必须牢记的关键因素。

sentences.en: I mean, wouldn't you agree?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你不同意吗？

sentences.en: I think absolute geography is destiny.
sentences.zh: 我认为地理绝对就是命运。

sentences.en: And actually, the geography, it's because of that geography that you have the ethnic mix.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正是因为这种地理环境，才形成了这种族群融合。

sentences.en: So the ethnic mix is a massive part of the story of modern Afghanistan, certainly.
sentences.zh: 因此，族群融合无疑是现代阿富汗历史中极其重要的一部分。

sentences.en: So Pashtuns, what are they, about 40%.
sentences.zh: 那么普什图人，大概占40%左右吧。

sentences.en: And then you've got Tajiks, Hazaras, Uzbeks, and other smaller groups of people.
sentences.zh: 然后还有塔吉克人、哈扎拉人、乌兹别克人以及其他较小的群体。

sentences.en: So in other words, it's not one homogenous kind of community of Afghans.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，阿富汗并非一个单一均质的阿富汗人群体。

sentences.en: It is competing people who speak different languages.
sentences.zh: 它是操着不同语言、相互竞争的人群。

sentences.en: And often, you know, their antagonists are each other rather than outsiders, necessarily.
sentences.zh: 而且通常来说，他们的对手往往是彼此，而不一定总是外来者。

sentences.en: And that reflects the fact that it's a crossroads.
sentences.zh: 这也反映出它是一个十字路口。

sentences.en: And, you know, strategically absolutely key coming from all kinds of directions.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它在战略上绝对至关重要，各方势力从四面八方汇聚于此。

sentences.en: So India, we've mentioned, and it's kind of very obvious at the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们提到了印度，目前这也非常显眼。

sentences.en: But also, there are trade links to China, to the Stans, to the north, and I think crucially to Iran.
sentences.zh: 但同时，这里还有通往中国、北方“斯坦”诸国，以及我认为至关重要的伊朗的贸易路线。

sentences.en: So I think Persia is absolutely massive, massive influence.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得波斯的影响绝对是极其巨大的。

sentences.en: And if Ali Ansari was here, who did that kind of wonderful podcast for us on the ways that Persia has influenced history,
sentences.zh: 如果阿里·安萨里在这里——他之前为我们做过那期精彩的播客，探讨波斯如何影响历史——

sentences.en: I would have no doubt in saying that Persia is probably the kind of decisive influence on the way that what is now Afghanistan has evolved.
sentences.zh: 我毫无疑问会说，波斯很可能是对现今阿富汗演变起到决定性影响的力量。

sentences.en: And really, what is now Afghanistan first emerges into history with the great Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 事实上，现今的阿富汗最初是随着伟大的波斯帝国进入历史视野的。

sentences.en: So that's the empire of Cyrus the Great.
sentences.zh: 也就是居鲁士大帝的帝国。

sentences.en: Cyrus the Great, Darius the Great, emerges in the 6th century BC, endures until Alexander conquers it.
sentences.zh: 居鲁士大帝、大流士大帝，它在公元前6世纪崛起，一直持续到亚历山大征服它。

sentences.en: And Bactria, as I mentioned, is the kind of the northern lands that lie above the kind of central mountain range in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 而巴克特里亚，正如我所提到的，是位于阿富汗中部山脉上方的北部土地。

sentences.en: And then beyond that, Sogdiana, into what's now Uzbekistan.
sentences.zh: 再往外是索格底亚那，延伸到现在的乌兹别克斯坦。

sentences.en: Those are satrapies or provinces of the great Persian king.
sentences.zh: 这些都是伟大波斯国王的总督辖区或省份。

sentences.en: And from the point of view of what happens when the Persian Empire falls, what's interesting about it is that it's a place where Greeks get exiled.
sentences.zh: 从波斯帝国灭亡后的情况来看，有趣的是，这里成了流放希腊人的地方。

sentences.en: So Miletus, the great city on the Aegean, on what's now Turkey, the Milesians rebel against the Persians, and the city gets destroyed.
sentences.zh: 比如米利都，爱琴海边上的伟大城市，位于现在的土耳其境内，米利都人反抗波斯人，结果城市被毁。

sentences.en: And the Milesians get exiled to Sogdiana, so north of Bactria.
sentences.zh: 米利都人被流放到索格底亚那，也就是巴克特里亚以北。

sentences.en: But other Greeks get exiled into Bactria.
sentences.zh: 但其他希腊人则被流放到巴克特里亚。

sentences.en: Into Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 也就是阿富汗。

sentences.en: It's what's now Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在的阿富汗。

sentences.en: So that's the sort of Siberia then.
sentences.zh: 所以那就是当时的西伯利亚了。

sentences.en: It's the sort of Persia's Siberia.
sentences.zh: 有点像是波斯的西伯利亚。

sentences.en: You get sent there if they're putting you out of harm's way as a sort of punishment.
sentences.zh: 如果你被送到那里，就说明他们为了以防万一而把你发配过去当一种惩罚。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And it means that, although, I mean, they become kind of loyal subjects of the Persian king.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，尽管——我的意思是，他们成了波斯国王的忠实臣民。

sentences.en: And the Bactrians, you know, people talk about how Afghanistan is a land that is the graveyard of empires.
sentences.zh: 而且巴克特里亚人，你知道，人们总说阿富汗是帝国的坟墓。

sentences.en: It isn't the graveyard of Persian imperialism.
sentences.zh: 但它可不是波斯帝国主义的坟墓。

sentences.en: I mean, it remains a part of the Persian empire for two centuries, basically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上它在两个世纪里一直是波斯帝国的一部分。

sentences.en: Which is why when Alexander turns up, he takes for granted that now that he is the great king, he's conquered the Persian empire, these lands belong to him.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，当亚历山大出现时，他理所当然地认为，既然自己已经是伟大的国王、征服了波斯帝国，这些土地自然就属于他。

sentences.en: Well, so this is an amazing story, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当惊人的故事，不是吗？

sentences.en: So Alexander has conquered Egypt, the Levant, the Persian heartland.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大已经征服了埃及、累范特和波斯的核心地区。

sentences.en: And the Persian king, Darius, has been killed.
sentences.zh: 波斯国王大流士已经被杀。

sentences.en: And the guy who killed him, Bessus, his base is in Bactria.
sentences.zh: 而杀死他的贝苏斯，其大本营就在巴克特里亚。

sentences.en: And he's shot off to Bactria and says, I'm the great king now.
sentences.zh: 他逃到了巴克特里亚并宣称：我现在是伟大的国王了。

sentences.en: And he goes off to his heartland, sort of over the Afghan mountains.
sentences.zh: 于是他回到了自己的大本营，也就是阿富汗群山的那一边。

sentences.en: And Alexander does what most normal people would say, I've finished now.
sentences.zh: 而亚历山大则做了大多数正常人会做的事：我到此为止了。

sentences.en: I'm the great king.
sentences.zh: 我是伟大的国王了。

sentences.en: I should go and enjoy myself in the palace.
sentences.zh: 我该去宫殿里享福了。

sentences.en: But Alexander follows him, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 但亚历山大还是追了上去，对吧？

sentences.en: He goes all the way over the mountains, past Kabul, this crazy expedition.
sentences.zh: 他翻山越岭，越过喀布尔，进行了一场疯狂的远征。

sentences.en: And captures Bessus.
sentences.zh: 并俘获了贝苏斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, which in complete contravention to everything that you read in the newspapers is a roaring success, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，这与你在报纸上读到的一切完全相反，这是一次巨大的成功，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it takes him a very long time, but he wins.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，虽然花了很长时间，但他确实赢了。

sentences.en: Yes, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，他赢了。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实赢了。

sentences.en: And also, with the modesty for which he's famed, he founds an enormous number of cities, all named Alexander after himself.
sentences.zh: 而且，秉承着他一贯的“谦逊”，他建立了一大批城市，全都以他自己的名字命名为亚历山大。

sentences.en: Some of which are, you know, famous cities to this day.
sentences.zh: 其中有些城市至今仍然是著名的城市。

sentences.en: So Kandahar is one of the cities that he founded.
sentences.zh: 坎大哈就是他建立的城市之一。

sentences.en: Is that Alexandria in Aracosia?
sentences.zh: 那是阿拉霍西亚的亚历山大城吗？

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But Kandahar, obviously, Sikanda, you know, you can see the kind of the derivation.
sentences.zh: 但坎大哈，显然，斯坎达，你能看出这种词源演变。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Ghazni, which becomes a crucial, a really, really important city in the early years of the Muslim conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 加兹尼，它后来成了穆斯林征服初期一个至关重要、极为重要的城市。

sentences.en: That's Alexandria in Opiana.
sentences.zh: 那是奥皮亚纳的亚历山大城。

sentences.en: Even beyond Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 甚至超出了阿富汗的范围。

sentences.en: So further north, you've got Alexandria, Eskate, Alexandria the furthest, which is kind of the outer limits of Greek civilization.
sentences.zh: 再往北，你有最远的亚历山大城，也就是希腊文明的最外围边界。

sentences.en: And then you have this city, Alexandria on the Oxus, which after Alexander has died and his general Seleucus takes over the kind of the vast bulk of the Persian Empire.
sentences.zh: 然后还有这座“氧化水上的亚历山大城”，在亚历山大死后，他的将军塞琉古接管了波斯帝国的绝大部分领土。

sentences.en: There's this kind of renegade satrap who basically casts off his loyalty to the distant Seleucid Empire and establishes this kingdom,
sentences.zh: 当时有一个叛变的总督，他基本上抛弃了对遥远的塞琉古帝国的忠诚，建立了一个王国，

sentences.en: this Bactrian Greek kingdom that survives for centuries.
sentences.zh: 这个希腊-巴克特里亚王国延续了几个世纪之久。

sentences.en: And actually is independent long after Greece and the Macedonian realms have been conquered by the Romans.
sentences.zh: 甚至在希腊和马其顿本土被罗马人征服很久之后，它依然保持独立。

sentences.en: And this is, yes, it's like something from a video game, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这简直就像电子游戏里的情节，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's like something from a strategy game.
sentences.zh: 就像策略游戏里的场景。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's like a science fiction story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这更像是一个科幻故事。

sentences.en: It's kind of like those science fiction stories where there are Earth colonists on Mars and then the Earth blows up and you've only got this colony left.
sentences.zh: 有点像那种科幻小说，地球殖民者到了火星，然后地球爆炸了，只剩下这个殖民地孤立存在。

sentences.en: So there's this amazing city that they found, I think, in the 70s that were being excavated by French archaeologists when the Soviets invaded in 1979 and they had to stop.
sentences.zh: 所以在70年代左右，他们发现了这座神奇的城市，当时法国考古学家正在进行发掘，结果1979年苏联入侵，他们不得不停止。

sentences.en: And then they went back in the 90s and again, they had to stop.
sentences.zh: 然后在90年代他们又回去了，但再次被迫停止。

sentences.en: But it's this extraordinary Greek city.
sentences.zh: 不过这是一座非凡的希腊城市。

sentences.en: So that's in the, looking at the map, it's the kind of the northeast region of what is now Afghanistan in the shadow of the mountains.
sentences.zh: 看地图的话，它位于现代阿富汗的东北部地区，依偎在群山的阴影之下。

sentences.en: And it's this great Greek city with theatres and with temples.
sentences.zh: 这是一座拥有剧院和神庙的伟大的希腊城市。

sentences.en: It's kind of an amazing image of Kibale, who fans of the World Cup of Gods will remember the worst wedding of all time.
sentences.zh: 这让人联想到库柏勒的形象，熟悉《诸神世界杯》的粉丝们会记得那场史上最糟糕的婚礼。

sentences.en: So she's portrayed.
sentences.zh: 她就是这样被描绘的。

sentences.zh: 这是阿伊哈努姆吗？

sentences.en: Is it called Ikanum?
sentences.zh: 它叫阿伊哈努姆吗？

sentences.en: That's right, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: Which means Lady Moon in Uzbek, apparently.
sentences.zh: 在乌兹别克语里，这似乎是“月亮夫人”的意思。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: And they found, have they found bilingual coins I read?
sentences.zh: 我读到过，他们是不是发现了双语硬币？

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: So half in, one side is in Greek and the other side is in a sacred Buddhist language or something.
sentences.zh: 硬币的一面是希腊语，另一面是某种神圣的佛教语言之类的。

sentences.en: Well, what also happens is that that gets destroyed, I think, in 140, something like that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，另外发生的事情是，这座城市大概在公元前140年左右被毁了。

sentences.en: But there is another, there's a kind of Indian Greek kingdom that has, is now in what's northern Pakistan,
sentences.zh: 但还有一个印度-希腊王国，现在位于巴基斯坦北部，

sentences.en: but, but includes a lot of what is currently Afghanistan and in complex ways that I would not want to tease out because I'm really not qualified to do it.
